$comment: D-LIR-OUTGOING-ARG-CURSOR-SPLIT-BETWEEN-TWO-PASSES-COLLIDES. A stacked SCALAR argument immediately followed by a stacked by-value AGGREGATE in ONE call. `lowerWideCallArgs` placed the scalars and REMOVED them from the Call; `lir_callconv` then placed the aggregate from a cursor of its own, which restarted at 0 because the scalars were no longer in the operand list to advance it — so both wrote the SAME outgoing-argument bytes and the scalar was destroyed before the call, silently, on both shipped pipelines. The repair is that ONE pass owns every outgoing byte offset: `lowerWideCallArgs` STATES the aggregate's offset on its carrier and stamps the Call, and callconv READS it and refuses to place anything itself. The route in is a function POINTER because HIR->MIR refuses the CALLEE of this shape (D-FC12-VARIADIC-OVERFLOW-FIXED-AGGREGATE-STACK-ARGS residual), so the callee is spelled in SCALARS with a byte-identical incoming layout and the observation is what the CALLEE actually read.
$commentRedOnDisable: Exit code is a bit mask: 1 = the stacked scalar the aggregate overwrote, 2 = the aggregate's first eightbyte, 4 = its second, 8 = the earlier stacked scalars, 16 = the register-passed arguments, 32 = the ALL-SCALAR CONTROL. Restore the two-cursor scheme (callconv placing the aggregate from its own `stackCursor.placeNamedAggregate` instead of reading the stated offset) and the subject bits go red while bit 32 stays CLEAN — the control reaches the SAME callee over the SAME eleven incoming positions with every argument a scalar, so its cleanliness is what shows the red is the interleave and not the harness.
$commentTargetGating: No pe64 arm, and the reason is structural rather than a platform gap: routing a by-value aggregate WHOLE to the outgoing area requires `!slotAligned` (hir_to_mir's `routeToStack`), and ms_x64 IS slot-aligned — a Win64 caller passes a 16-byte struct BY POINTER, so this interleave cannot arise there and a pe64 arm would be asserting a different ABI's layout under this row's name. The three declared arms still COMPILE on every host (the in-process runner compiles a `runOn`-excluded spec and only skips the spawn), so a Windows gate still witnesses the emission.
